newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany looking into fate of Iranian journalist.
newsitem.headline: Germany looking into fate of Iranian journalist.

text.p: The German Foreign Ministry said on Wednesday its embassy in Tehran was looking into the whereabouts of an Iranian journalist amid fresh allegations he had been arrested by the Iranian secret service en route to Germany.

Former Iranian President Abolhassan Banisadr said earlier on Wednesday the journalist, Faraj Sarkuhi, had been arrested by the secret service in Tehran just before he was due to board an airplane bound for Germany on November 3.
"The embassy is looking into the matter," said a Foreign Ministry spokeswoman, who declined to make any further comment.
Tehran newspaper Jomhui Eslami said last week that Sarkuhi had boarded the plane and was now in Germany.

The daily said flight information from state airline Iran Air showed that Sarkuhi, editor of the monthly Adineh (Friday), was issued a ticket and a boarding card and that "he definitely arrived at Hamburg airport at 1430 hours (1330 GMT) on Sunday (November 3)".
An official at Iran Air in Frankfurt said the airline could not release any information about its passengers.

Banisadr, in separate interviews in the newspaper Frankfurter Rundschau and for Berlin broadcaster Inforadio, said Sarkuhi had never left Iran. He said Sarkuhi was being held by Iranian secret police in an appartment in Tehran.
He gave the address of the apartment as Number 7, Avenue Pasdaran.
"He is in isolation and is being interrogated," Banisadr told Inforadio.

Mehdi Khanbaba Tehrani, an Iranian journalist living in Germany, claimed earlier this month that Sarkuhi was taken into custody by the Iranian secret service as he was boarding a plane bound for Germany to visit his wife and child.

Tehrani, spokesman for the Union of Iranian Authors in Exile, said Sarkuhi's newspaper received an anonymous phone call shortly after he disappeared from someone claiming that Sarkuhi had been detained because his papers were not in order.
